reference_items.figure_description: A geometric diagram showing a straight horizontal line with points A, O, and B labeled from left to right, where O is between A and B. Three rays emanate upwards from point O into the upper half-plane: ray ON (pointing up and to the left), ray OC (pointing almost straight up, slightly to the right), and ray OM (pointing up and to the right). reference_items.stem:
The diagram shows a system for locating points

[Image: A group of 6 concentric circles with origin “O”. Degrees from 0 to 360 are marked in 10 degree intervals where 0 and 360 are marked on a line “A” that goes across all circles. The 6 concentric circles are labeled from 1 to 6 along line “A”.]

In this system, the position of a point P is described by its distance from origin, O, and the amount of counterclockwise turn from a baseline OA to OP. Thus, the coordinates of P are (5, 340°).

A. Mark the points B (3, 30°) and C (4, 120°) on the graph above.
B. Draw the angle BOC. What is the measure of angle BOC?

Angle BOC = ____°

descriptors: Both points correctly marked (pictured on right) [Image: A line drawn from O to B where B is the point where the third circle intersects the 30 degree mark. Figure also has a line drawn from O to C where C is the point where the fourth circle intersects the 120 degree mark.]
One point correctly marked
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Correct value given for incorrect point(s) drawn in A
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: Two score points will be given if both parts A and B are correct. One score point will be given if only part A is correct. No credit is given if only part B is correct.
reference_items.figure_description: A circular polar coordinate grid centered at an origin O, formed by 6 concentric circles. A horizontal baseline ray extends right from O, labeled A at its end, with the 6 concentric circles labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 along this ray. Radial line segments extend from O every 10° around the full circle, labeled on the outer rim counterclockwise from 0° at ray OA through 10°, 20°, 30°, up to 350°. A point labeled P is plotted on the 5th circle along the 340° radial line.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines with arrows at both ends are labeled m (top line) and n (bottom line). Two intersecting lines cross lines m and n: one line slopes upward from lower left to upper right, and the other slopes downward from upper left to lower right. The two lines intersect each other at a single point on line m, and they cross line n at two separate points, forming a triangle between lines m and n. The top interior angle of this triangle at the intersection point on line m is marked with an arc and labeled b°. The bottom-right interior angle of the triangle along line n is marked with an arc and labeled 70°. Above line m, in the angle between the right side of line m and the upward-sloping line, the angle is marked with an arc and labeled 60°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
